terms.gloss: give someone a share of something
evidence: Cic. Lael. 70: impertiant ea suīs commūnicentque cum proximīs
terms.comment: Beside commūnicāre (to have or use a thing in common with someone), impertīre is to hand some of it over.

phrases.latin: Pilam cum amīcō commūnicā; ūnā lūdite.
phrases.english: Share the ball with your friend; play together.

phrases.latin: ut, sī quam praestantiam virtūtis, ingeniī, fortūnae cōnsecūtī sint, impertiant ea suīs commūnicentque cum proximīs
phrases.english: that if they have gained any distinction of character, talent, or fortune, they should give their own people a part of it and share it with those closest to them
He shares the reward with them

sources: Lewis & Short: communico · Lewis & Short: impertio
